title: Cyclone Murasu to cross Andhra coast near Ongole late Monday as severe storm, IMD says
dek: The IMD expects landfall between 11.30 pm on 2 November and 4 am on 3 November, with winds gusting to 120 kmph and a storm surge of up to 1.5 m. Bengal faces only light rain, but Kolkata and Haldia ports have raised their storm signal.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Cyclonic Storm Murasu was about 420 km east-southeast of Chennai at 5.30 pm IST on Sunday and is expected to strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by early Monday, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said. It is forecast to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, close to Ongole, between about 11.30 pm on Monday, 2 November, and 4 am on Tuesday, 3 November, with sustained winds of 100 to 110 kmph gusting to 120 kmph.

The IMD warned of a storm surge of 1 to 1.5 metres above the astronomical tide in low-lying areas of south coastal Andhra Pradesh at landfall, with the highest surge expected over Bapatla and parts of Guntur, Krishna and Prakasam districts. Murasu, a Tamil word for a drum, is the second cyclone to threaten the Andhra coast in a week, after Cyclone Arnab. There is still no weather warning for West Bengal, but the distant warning signal at the Kolkata and Haldia ports has been raised.

## Latest bulletin

According to a special bulletin issued at 10 pm on Sunday by the IMD's Regional Meteorological Centre in Kolkata, Murasu lay near latitude 12.7°N and longitude 84.1°E at 5.30 pm, about 420 km east-southeast of Chennai, 490 km east-southeast of Nellore, 500 km southeast of Machilipatnam, 530 km southeast of Ongole and 560 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam. It had moved west-northwest at about 25 kmph over the previous six hours.

The bulletin's track table shows winds of 90-100 kmph, gusting to 110 kmph, by 11.30 pm on Sunday, rising to 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph, by midday on Monday as the storm turns northwest towards the coast. After landfall it is forecast to weaken quickly over land, to a cyclonic storm by 5.30 am on Tuesday, a deep depression by Tuesday evening and a depression by Wednesday morning, as it moves north over Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

The IMD's national bulletin issued on Sunday evening forecast heavy to very heavy rain at a few places and extremely heavy rain at isolated places over coastal Andhra Pradesh on 2 and 3 November, heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places in Rayalaseema and Tamil Nadu, and isolated extremely heavy rain in Telangana on 3 November. South Odisha may get heavy rain on 2 November and heavy to very heavy rain on 3 and 4 November.

Gale winds of 80-90 kmph, gusting to 100 kmph, are expected along and off the Andhra coast from Monday evening, rising to 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph, from Monday midnight until Tuesday noon. Winds of 60-70 kmph are likely along the north Tamil Nadu and Puducherry coast from Monday evening. Fishing is suspended along the Andhra coast from Monday morning to Wednesday afternoon.

The IMD has warned of local flooding, waterlogging, disruption to road and rail traffic, damage to thatched and kutcha houses, uprooted trees and damage to banana, papaya and coconut plantations, and asked authorities to move people out of vulnerable coastal settlements. An IMD scientist, Bharathi Savabi, told PTI earlier on Sunday that extremely heavy rain is likely in Krishna, Guntur and Bapatla districts.

## How the storm grew

The system was a depression about 960 km east-southeast of Chennai at 5.30 pm on Saturday. It became a deep depression overnight and was named Cyclonic Storm Murasu at 11.30 am IST on Sunday, the IMD said. Since then it has moved steadily west-northwest at 20 to 27 kmph, and the IMD has narrowed the expected landfall from a broad stretch of coast to the area around Ongole.

## What it means for Bengal

The Kolkata bulletin says there is "at present no weather warning for West Bengal" linked to Murasu, which it is keeping under continuous watch. Distant Warning Signal No. 2 has now been hoisted at the Kolkata and Haldia ports, up from the Distant Cautionary Signal No. 1 hoisted on Saturday, with sectional signals II and IV at Sagar Island. A distant signal warns ships leaving port of a storm far out at sea; it does not indicate danger to the port itself.

Light rain or thundershowers are likely in south Bengal on Monday and Tuesday, with light to moderate rain at one or two places in North 24 Parganas, Kolkata, Howrah, Hooghly and the Midnapore districts on 3 November, and dry weather from 4 November, the bulletin said. Habibur Rahman Biswas, director of the regional meteorological centre at Alipore, earlier told ETV Bharat Bangla that the five northern hill and Dooars districts may see light rain on Tuesday.

There is no fishing warning for the Bengal coast, but the IMD has advised Bengal's fishermen not to go towards the west-central and adjoining northwest Bay of Bengal or the south Odisha coast from 2 to 4 November.

## Odisha and the south brace again

Southern Odisha is still recovering from Cyclone Arnab, which brought extreme rain of up to 546 mm at Patrapur in Ganjam district and forced tens of thousands of people from their homes, Pragativadi reported. The IMD expects squally winds of 40-50 kmph, gusting to 60 kmph, along and off the south Odisha coast from Monday evening, rising to 50-60 kmph, gusting to 70 kmph, on Tuesday, with rough to very rough seas until Wednesday afternoon.

IMD Bhubaneswar has issued an orange warning for heavy to very heavy rain in Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Gajapati and Ganjam on 3 and 4 November, Argus reported. In Ganjam, officials were told to move people out of flood-prone, low-lying areas by Saturday night and to pre-position food, drinking water and generators in villages likely to flood, with NDRF and Odisha disaster response teams being stationed in sensitive areas, according to Pragativadi. Schools across Ganjam will stay shut until 3 November, The News Insight reported. Ganjam's fishermen have been told not to go to sea from 2 to 4 November.

Tamil Nadu's regional meteorological centre expects rain across the state from 1 to 6 November, and Kerala has yellow alerts in several districts from Sunday to Wednesday.

## Background

Murasu is the second cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal this season after Arnab, which has since weakened over southeast Uttar Pradesh. The IMD has named a wide stretch of coast for now and usually narrows the landfall point as a storm approaches and its track becomes clearer.

## What happens next

The IMD expects Murasu to become a severe cyclonic storm early on Monday and to approach the coast through the day. Ports and fishermen along the Andhra, Tamil Nadu and Odisha coasts should follow the IMD's district and port warnings, which will be revised as the storm nears land. The Kolkata centre said its next update for Bengal would be issued on Monday.

## Key numbers

- Landfall: south Andhra coast between Nellore and Narsapur, close to Ongole, between about 11.30 pm on 2 November and 4 am on 3 November
- Peak forecast wind: 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph
- Storm surge: 1-1.5 m above astronomical tide in low-lying south coastal Andhra Pradesh
- Distance from Chennai: about 960 km at 5.30 pm Saturday; about 420 km at 5.30 pm Sunday
- Named: Cyclonic Storm Murasu, 11.30 am IST, 1 November
- Bengal: no warning; Distant Warning Signal No. 2 at Kolkata and Haldia ports
